I read the whole file (lines 1–91). It has two parallel blocks, one for curve11a2 and one for curve37a1. Each block has an equation_iff theorem, a Δ simp lemma, a c₄ simp lemma and an IsElliptic instance. The repeated proofs are all short.

- The equation_iff proofs repeat `rw [Affine.equation_iff]`, then a `simp only` unfolding of baseChange and map lemmas, then `constructor <;> intro h <;> linear_combination h`. This is routine unfolding plus a one-line ring identity. The two simp lists also differ (`map_ofNat` appears in only one), so a shared lemma would need hypotheses about the coefficient images. Stating that lemma would cost about as much as the proofs it replaces.
- The Δ and c₄ proofs are single `simp [Δ, b₂, ...]` calls, which are short calculations.
- The IsElliptic instances are a three-step rewrite followed by `norm_num`, which is a thin wrapper over existing API.

None of this is nontrivial mathematical reasoning repeated in a way the rubric counts. A helper lemma would not clearly improve readability or maintenance. The remaining uncertainty is that I did not check whether Mathlib has a more general coefficient-based equation lemma. Even if it does, that would be an API-reuse point, not repeated proof machinery.
